author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 여름철새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록
summary: 해마다 수십 마리가 찾아오는 여름철새이며, 겨울에도 드물게 기록된다. 암컷이 구애하고 과시 행동을 하며, 봄부터 가을 사이에 한배에 알 4~6개를 낳아 수컷에게 품게 한 뒤 새 수컷과 다시 짝을 지어 알을 낳는다. 곤충, 조개, 지렁이와 볏과 식물, 여러 풀씨를 먹는 잡식성이다. 아프리카, 아시아, 오스트레일리아에 분포한다.

sexes.male: 암컷보다 작고 빛깔이 덜 선명하며, 목과 윗가슴에 회색 세로무늬가 있다.
sexes.female: 수컷보다 크고 빛깔이 선명하다. 갈색 머리에 넓은 흰 정수리선이 있고 목과 윗가슴은 밤색이다.

art.subject: Greater Painted-snipe (Rostratula benghalensis), adult female in the breeding season, as seen in Korean rice paddies from May to August: head, neck, throat and upper breast deep chestnut, the crown blackish with a narrow pale buff to whitish central stripe from the forehead to the hindcrown; a bold white ring around the eye extending back as a short white stripe behind it; a blackish band at the lower edge of the chestnut breast; underparts below it white, the white continuing up as a narrow strap around the bend of the folded wing onto the mantle; back and wing coverts dark bronzy olive-green, finely barred dark, with buff stripes along the edges of the mantle. Long pale orange-pink bill drooping slightly at the tip; dark eye; legs dull greenish-yellow.
art.pose: standing still at the muddy edge of a weedy paddy at dusk, side view
art.scene: Korean summer lowland: fallow and newly planted rice paddies with muddy edges, rank grass and rushes, evening light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult female, side view at a paddy edge: chestnut head, throat and neck with a narrow pale crown stripe and a bold white spectacle extending behind the eye, blackish breast band, white underparts with a white strap around the shoulder, dark bronzy-green finely barred back, long pale orange-pink bill drooping at the tip, greenish-yellow legs

adult male, side view standing: smaller and duller, grey-brown head, neck and upper breast with grey streaks, buff crown stripe and buff spectacle extending behind the eye, wing coverts boldly marked with large golden-buff spots and bars, white underparts and shoulder strap, pinkish-brown bill, greenish legs
art.build: Snipe-like but chunkier wader, about 23.5cm long, larger than a starling; female larger and brighter than the male. Rounded head, short neck, plump body. Bill clearly longer than the head, fairly stout, straight and drooping slightly at the tip. Legs medium length, greenish, with long toes. Short rounded tail; broad rounded wings; flight slow and rail-like with legs dangling. Mostly active at dusk, standing still at muddy edges.
avoid: Do not paint a long, straight snipe bill with a striped snipe head — that is Common Snipe; this bird has a drooping-tipped pinkish bill and a white spectacle.
Do not make the male brighter than the female; the female has the chestnut head and neck.
Do not paint a white throat on the female; her chin, throat and neck are chestnut down to the dark breast band.
Do not paint a broad white crown stripe; it is narrow and pale buff to whitish.
Do not omit the white strap curving up around the bend of the wing.
